answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by committing to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where marginal cost scales superlinearly as O(N^2). When an attacker tries to flood the network, each successive identity registration demands an escalating burnt deposit: the rate of cost increase, or delta, grows quadratically rather than staying flat. Unbonded ephemeral nodes collapse into an unviable dune of barren compute, leaving each valid agent identity anchored as an economically verifiable relic.
